pr_title: tls_provider_init(): Fix leaks in error cases
pr_comments: This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.3 and 3.2 branches. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: There is a memory leak defect on line 3226 of the file /openssl/test/tls-provider.c.
issue_context.body:
Triggering path of the defect:

1.On line 3220 of the file /openssl/test/tls-provider.c, a pointer variable named 'libctx' is defined and a dynamic memory area is allocated for it through the function OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_from_dispatch, as shown in the diagram below:
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_5.png

2.In line 436 of the OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_from_dispatch function, a pointer variable named 'ctx' is defined and dynamic memory is allocated for it through the function OSSL_LIB_CTX_new. Then, on line 446, this pointer is returned, as shown in the diagram below:
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_6.png

3.After the execution of the OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_from_dispatch function, a pointer named 'prov_ctx' is created on line 3223, and a dynamic memory area is allocated for it through the function xor_newprovctx. The variable 'libctx' is passed as a parameter to the xor_newprovctx function, as shown in the diagram below:
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_7.png

4.On line 437 of the xor_newprovctx function, a variable named 'prov_ctx' is defined, and dynamic memory is allocated for it through the function OPENSSL_malloc. Then, on line 447, it is returned, as shown in the diagram below:
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_8.png

5.After the execution of the xor_newprovctx function, if the if statement on line 3225 returns true, the program will return on line 3226. The condition of the if statement on line 3225 checks whether the pointer 'libctx' is NULL or 'prov_ctx' is NULL. In this scenario, there is a possibility that the dynamic memory area pointed to by 'libctx' is not NULL while the dynamic memory area pointed to by 'prov_ctx' is NULL. In this case, there is a memory leak issue with the pointer 'libctx', as shown in the diagram below:
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_9.png

review_comments: pre-existing: missing space in front of the `=` on this line and the one above. Up to you if you want to fix this (now we're in the area, which is my fault, sorry!)
Err, should this be `provctx = NULL` (without the `*`)? If `OPENSSL_free()` works the same as `free()`, this would be use-after-free
Please note that these are two different variables: `prov_ctx` and `provctx` - confusing I agree but I did not want to make larger changes in the code.
Oh wow, yes, that is absolutely horrible, I did not notice the `_`

I think a rename of `provctx` (the argument to the function) to `p_prov_ctx` (or something similar) would only be a change on 2 lines, and as a first commit in this PR (to be squashed on merge) might make this function more maintainable in the future - WDYT? Agree out-of-scope for "fix leak", but as this is so bad it seems worth fixing on a "tidy up the kitchen a little bit each time" basis.

Presumably we wouldn't need to change the name of the parameter in the function declaration if we did that? (I mean: we don't from a C perspective, but if there's something in the CI that checks argument names match in declarations and definitions we might need to)
I did it the other way around - renamed `prov_ctx` as we do not use the `p_something` convention often.
